concepts.name: Neuron structure and parts
concepts.summary: Name and describe the roles of the soma, dendrites, axon, myelin sheath and axon terminals.

concepts.name: Glial cell roles
concepts.summary: Recall that glia support neurons through insulation, metabolic support, immune defence and homeostasis.

concepts.name: Resting membrane potential
concepts.summary: Explain that neurons maintain a negative voltage across the membrane through ion gradients and the sodium-potassium pump.

concepts.name: Action potential sequence
concepts.summary: Describe the all-or-none spike as depolarisation, repolarisation and refractory recovery driven by ion flow.

concepts.name: Chemical synapse transmission
concepts.summary: Explain how an impulse triggers neurotransmitter release, receptor binding and a postsynaptic response.

concepts.name: Major neurotransmitters and roles
concepts.summary: Match glutamate, GABA, dopamine, serotonin and acetylcholine to their typical functions.

concepts.name: Central and peripheral nervous systems
concepts.summary: Distinguish the brain and spinal cord from peripheral nerves and the somatic and autonomic divisions.

concepts.name: Main brain regions and functions
concepts.summary: Link the cortex lobes, cerebellum, hippocampus, amygdala and brainstem to their broad functions.

misconceptions.text: Humans use only 10% of their brains.
Neurons physically touch each other and pass electrical current directly at every connection.
Glial cells are just passive filler with no role in brain function.

concepts.name: Ion channels and the Nernst potential
concepts.summary: Use ion concentration gradients to predict the direction of ion flow and equilibrium potentials for Na+ and K+.

concepts.name: Voltage-gated channel dynamics
concepts.summary: Apply channel opening and inactivation to explain the phases of the action potential and the refractory period.

concepts.name: Saltatory conduction
concepts.summary: Explain how myelin and nodes of Ranvier speed conduction and what happens in demyelination.

concepts.name: Excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potentials
concepts.summary: Predict whether a given neurotransmitter-receptor pair moves the membrane toward or away from threshold.

concepts.name: Ionotropic versus metabotropic receptors
concepts.summary: Contrast fast channel receptors with slower G-protein-coupled receptors in terms of speed and effect.

concepts.name: Sensory transduction and pathways
concepts.summary: Trace how a stimulus is converted to neural signals and relayed via the thalamus to primary sensory cortex.

concepts.name: Reflex arc and motor pathway
concepts.summary: Trace the path of a simple spinal reflex and distinguish upper from lower motor neurons.

concepts.name: Autonomic sympathetic and parasympathetic
concepts.summary: Predict bodily effects of sympathetic versus parasympathetic activation.

misconceptions.text: A stronger stimulus produces a bigger action potential.
Glutamate is always excitatory and GABA always inhibitory regardless of receptor type.
Sensory information from the body always goes to the cortex on the same side without crossing.

concepts.name: Synaptic integration
concepts.summary: Work out whether a neuron fires by combining spatial and temporal summation of inputs at the axon hillock.

concepts.name: Cable properties and length constant
concepts.summary: Analyse how membrane resistance, capacitance and axon diameter shape signal spread and conduction velocity.

concepts.name: Long-term potentiation and depression
concepts.summary: Analyse how NMDA receptor coincidence detection and AMPA receptor changes strengthen or weaken synapses.

concepts.name: Hebbian and spike-timing plasticity
concepts.summary: Apply the rule that correlated activity strengthens connections to predict synaptic changes.

concepts.name: Hippocampus and memory systems
concepts.summary: Distinguish memory types and match them to hippocampal, striatal, cerebellar and amygdala involvement using patient evidence such as H.M.

concepts.name: Basal ganglia and cerebellar motor control
concepts.summary: Contrast basal ganglia action selection with cerebellar error correction and relate them to Parkinson's disease and ataxia.

concepts.name: Cortical organisation and maps
concepts.summary: Use receptive fields, topographic maps and hierarchical visual processing to explain perception.

concepts.name: EEG and fMRI signal basis
concepts.summary: Analyse what EEG and fMRI BOLD actually measure and their trade-offs in temporal and spatial resolution.

misconceptions.text: Memories are stored in the hippocampus permanently.
The cerebellum is involved only in movement and the basal ganglia only in initiating movement.

concepts.name: Neural circuit motifs
concepts.summary: Analyse how feedforward, feedback and lateral inhibition and recurrent excitation shape circuit computation.

concepts.name: Systems consolidation and reconsolidation
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for hippocampal-neocortical transfer, replay during sleep and memory reconsolidation.

concepts.name: Neural coding schemes
concepts.summary: Compare rate, temporal and population codes and tuning curves as accounts of how information is represented.

concepts.name: Reward prediction error in dopamine
concepts.summary: Evaluate the claim that dopamine neurons encode reward prediction error and its role in basal ganglia learning.

concepts.name: Amygdala and emotional learning
concepts.summary: Analyse amygdala circuits in fear conditioning and extinction and their interaction with prefrontal cortex.

concepts.name: Experimental design in neuroimaging
concepts.summary: Evaluate the validity of neuroimaging claims, including reverse inference, multiple comparisons and confounds.

concepts.name: Causal tools: lesions, stimulation, optogenetics
concepts.summary: Evaluate which manipulation or recording method best supports a causal claim about a circuit.

concepts.name: Perceptual inference and attention
concepts.summary: Analyse how top-down signals and attention modulate sensory processing and perceptual illusions.

misconceptions.text: Dopamine is simply the brain's pleasure chemical.
If a brain region activates during a task, it must be the region for that mental process.
Perception is a passive bottom-up readout of sensory input.

concepts.name: Computational models of neurons
concepts.summary: Build and fit conductance-based or simplified spiking models to explain or predict neural dynamics.

concepts.name: Network models of memory
concepts.summary: Design network models such as attractors or complementary learning systems that capture plasticity and memory phenomena.

concepts.name: Critique of neuroscience evidence
concepts.summary: Evaluate claims for statistical power, circularity, small samples and generalisation from animal models to humans.

concepts.name: Neural population dynamics
concepts.summary: Evaluate analyses that infer computation from low-dimensional population activity.

concepts.name: Experiment design for circuits
concepts.summary: Design experiments combining recording, perturbation and behaviour to test competing circuit hypotheses.

concepts.name: Homeostatic and structural plasticity
concepts.summary: Evaluate how homeostatic mechanisms, critical periods and adult neurogenesis stabilise or reshape circuits.

concepts.name: Integrating theories of cognition
concepts.summary: Compare theoretical frameworks such as predictive coding and Bayesian inference against empirical evidence.

concepts.name: Translational neurotherapeutics
concepts.summary: Propose mechanism-based interventions for disorders using knowledge of circuits, receptors and neuromodulation.

misconceptions.text: A model that fits the data well proves the brain implements that mechanism.
Findings in rodents transfer directly to human brain function and treatment.
Low-dimensional population structure shows the brain computes in that space rather than reflecting analysis choices.
